name: Frankincense
overview: Frankincense holds a significant role in the Old Testament sacrificial system, serving as a key ingredient in sacred anointing oils and as a fragrant offering burned on the altar. It was placed upon meat offerings and showbread, symbolizing a pleasing aroma to the LORD, as described in Leviticus 2 and Exodus 30. However, frankincense was expressly prohibited in certain sin offerings involving turtledoves or pigeons, highlighting the distinct treatment of sin offerings compared to other sacrifices (Leviticus 5). Through its use as incense and in memorial offerings, frankincense underscores the holiness and reverence required in worshiping God.
